links.outcome: Age-related entity retention and hallucination in LLM summaries across child, adult, and older adult groups
links.effect: Systematic disparities across models and age groups. Demographic fidelity was lowest for adult-focused summaries, and under-represented populations were more prone to hallucinations. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
links.quote: Our results reveal systematic disparities across models and age groups: demographic fidelity is lowest for adult-focused summaries, and under-represented populations are more prone to hallucinations.

unlisted_practices: Demographic Salience Score (DSS) metric for age-related entity retention and hallucination in summarisation

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating demographic bias and demographic information retention (specifically age) of LLMs in biomedical evidence synthesis workflows.
